technology.title: Will on-device AI pressure IT OLED developers to accelerate the adoption of next-generation OLED technologies?
technology.desc: In recent years, the main focus of the OLED industry was on reducing power consumption. OLED developers introduced several novel technologies, including new backplanes, materials and device architectures, to increase device and system efficiency. This article looks into the potential pressure that the acceleration of on-device AI (locally running AI engines as opposed cloud-based AI) will have on OLED developers to reduce the power consumption even further, especially within the laptop segment, and adopt novel next-gen technologies. Every generation of on-device AI silicon asks for more power than the last. Model sizes on flagship devices have gone from roughly 100M parameters in 2020 to 3–7B today, with 13–20B expected on premium hardware by 2028. Each doubling roughly doubles compute and memory-bandwidth demand. NPUs are dramatically more efficient than running the same workload on a CPU or GPU, but they still consume a lot of power. When we analyze the power consumption of devices, there are four main components: batteries, the main chipset, the radio, and the display.Improving the battery capacity is of course an excellent option - but improvement in battery technologies has been slow. There are some encouraging signs, though. Silicon-carbon anodes are already shipping in over 10% of smartphones, and solid-state cells are likely only 2–3 years from premium smartphones. But it is expected that energy density gains will be a step change, and not a dramatic improvement overnight.Another important component is the chipset, where process node efficiency brings real gains. TSMC's N2 transition to gate-all-around transistors for example may bring about 30% improvement over the company's 2023 process. The radio is another important power customer. As people get used to downloading huge amount of data over 5G networks, the power demands are rising too. We are seeing improvement in analog/digital radio design, but these are not drastic. New communication protocols can result in dramatic power savings - but these take years to mature.The fourth main device power +component is the display. In the past 10 years we've seen dramatic increases in the power consumption of OLED displays.

technology.title: Skin-like test models could help improve medical devices for people of all skin tones
technology.desc: Researchers have developed realistic skin-mimicking models that could help improve the accuracy of optical medical devices and wearable sensors across a wider range of skin tones. The multilayer silicone phantoms incorporate artificial blood vessels and simulated blood flow, enabling controlled testing of technologies such as pulse oximeters. The team found that coffee more closely replicated the optical properties of skin pigmentation than commercial skin-tone pigments, producing reflectance spectra of multi-layered phantoms that better matched human skin. Imaging experiments showed that darker pigmented layers increasingly masked signals from underlying blood vessels, reflecting a known challenge for light-based health measurements. The durable phantoms may provide a valuable tool for reducing skin-tone-related bias in the development and evaluation of optical healthcare technologies.

world.title: Pesticide Poisoning Suspected in Deaths of 15 Kenya Elephants
world.desc:
The deaths of 15 elephants outside Kenya's Amboseli National Park have sparked concern. The Kenya Wildlife Service said preliminary findings suggest they may have been poisoned by cyanide-containing pesticides used on nearby tomato farms.
Wildlife officials found traces of cyanide in samples from some elephants and said the animals showed signs consistent with poisoning. Investigations are continuing, and deliberate poisoning has not been ruled out.
Conservationists and local farmers have questioned the pesticide theory. They said that elephants would have had to consume large quantities and that other wildlife sharing the same habitat was unaffected. The incident has also renewed concerns over illegal agrochemicals, weak enforcement of pesticide regulations and growing human-wildlife conflict as farming expands into elephant migration corridors.
